issues.span: Should the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha be seen
issues.evidence: Tibetan ends བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྙམ་མམ, "do you think ... should be seen", a question to Subhūti about his thought (continuing 8-1 ཇི་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས); Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-68 paraphrases it as བལྟ་བ་སྟེ་གཟུང་བར་བྱ་སྙམ་མམ ("do you think ... to be taken as"). The English drops the སྙམ་ ("think") element.
issues.fix: Do you think the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha should be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great man?

issues.span: and if someone were to take up even just a four-line verse ... that person would generate on that basis far greater, incalculable, immeasurable merit
issues.evidence: Tibetan is a comparison: ལུས་ ... ཡོངས་སུ་གཏོང་བ་བས། ("than giving away bodies ...") གང་གིས་ ... བཟུང་སྟེ་ ... ཡང་དག་པར་བསྟན་ན། དེ་ཉིད་ ... བསོད་ནམས་ཆེས་མང་དུ ... བསྐྱེད་ ("whoever takes up ... and teaches ... generates far more merit"). Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-69: ལུས་ཀྱི་སྦྱིན་པ་ ... བཏང་བ་ལས་ཀྱང༌། ... བཟུང་ ... བསོད་ནམས་ལྷག་པར་ཆེའོ (merit greater than that of giving the body). The English makes two parallel "if" clauses, so "far greater" has no stated standard of comparison.
issues.fix: Subhūti, if some man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand of the Gaṅgā river, someone who takes up even just a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse and teaches it properly to others would, on that basis, generate far greater merit than that, incalculable and immeasurable.

issues.evidence: ངོ་མཚར་རབ་དང་ལྡན་པ is the same expression rendered "supreme marvel" in 8-11 and ངོ་མཚར་ is "marvel" in 8-9, 8-14; here it is "wonder", so one Tibetan term has two renderings across adjacent segments.
ངོ་མཚར་རབ་དང་ལྡན་པ is rendered "supreme marvel" in 8-11 (and "marvel" for ངོ་མཚར in 8-9, 8-14), but "wonder" here.
issues.fix: will be endowed with supreme marvel
